points.t: Rough papule with black dots that **interrupts the skin lines**: hands, feet, around nails.
HPV infects basal keratinocytes → hyperkeratosis. Spread by contact, fomites, autoinoculation.
Reassure, or salicylic acid daily after paring for 8–12 weeks, ± cryotherapy.
A fast-growing or ulcerating ‘wart’, especially if immunosuppressed, may be SCC. Refer.

cause.lead: A virus that makes the top layers of skin pile up.
points: **HPV** (double-stranded DNA). Common cutaneous types: 1, 2, 3, 4, 10, 27, 29, 57.
Infects **basal keratinocytes** → hyperkeratosis and new virus.
**Spread**: skin contact, pools and changing rooms, **autoinoculation** (a line along a scratch: pseudo-Koebner).
Incubation weeks to months. More warts with dermatitis or **immunosuppression**.

visuals.caption: Normal skin (left) and a common wart (right): virus enters through a small break, infects the basal layer, and the epidermis folds upward under a thick cap of keratin, with capillaries rising into it.
visuals.alt: Skin cross-section through a viral wart with virus particles in the basal layer

features.lead: Match the look to the site.
points: **Rough, hyperkeratotic** papule.
**Black or red dots**: thrombosed capillaries.
Breaks the normal **skin lines** (corns do not).
Often several; may line up along a scratch.

visuals.caption: Plantar wart (left): skin lines stop at its edge and go round it, with black capillary dots. Corn (right): skin lines run straight through a smooth central core.
visuals.alt: Magnified sole skin comparing a plantar wart and a corn

items.name: Common
items.t: Rough hyperkeratotic papules with capillary dots.

items.name: Plane
items.t: Flat-topped, skin-coloured, numerous; spread by shaving.

items.name: Filiform
items.t: Thin fronds on a narrow base.

items.name: Periungual
items.t: Around or under the nail; nail dystrophy risk.

points: **Clinical** diagnosis.
Paring shows pinpoint bleeding or black dots; dermoscopy helps.
**Wart**: tender when squeezed **from the sides**.
**Corn**: tender on **direct pressure**; skin lines run through.
Immunosuppression (transplant, HIV), dermatitis.
Diabetes or neuropathy changes treatment choice.
Usually **none**.
**Biopsy** if SCC is a concern, especially if immunosuppressed.

cards.name: Corn / callus
cards.clue: Pressure site; skin lines continue through; no capillary dots.

cards.name: SCC / keratoacanthoma
cards.clue: Rapid growth, ulceration or tenderness; older or immunosuppressed. **Refer**.

manage.lead: Many resolve alone: about half of childhood warts in 6 months, most within 2 years.

points: Treat only if painful, disabling, immunosuppressed, or the patient prefers.
Flip-flops in communal showers; no shared towels; cover verrucae for swimming.

rx.drug: Salicylic acid paint, gel or plaster
rx.note: Protect surrounding skin. Avoid in diabetes or poor sensation.
Blistering, pain, pigment change (more in skin of colour); mind superficial nerves.

points: Curettage or electrosurgery (scarring), radiofrequency, CO₂ laser.
Intralesional bleomycin, contact immunotherapy (diphencyprone), microwave (plantar).
Podophyllin or imiquimod: better evidence for anogenital warts.

limits.t: No treatment ‘kills’ HPV instantly; recurrence is common until immunity clears it.
Mixed evidence: optional add-on, not a cure.
No self-treatment with salicylic acid or cryotherapy.

items.t: Rapid growth, bleeding, ulceration or atypical look: consider **SCC**.
**Immunosuppressed** with extensive or recalcitrant warts → dermatology.
Extensive facial or periungual warts where destruction risks scarring or nail damage.
Diabetes, neuropathy or vascular disease: no self-treatment on the feet.

pearls.t: Set expectations: weeks of daily treatment; recurrence is common.
Periungual warts: avoid aggressive destruction near the **nail matrix**.
Prevention: flip-flops, own towel, cover verrucae for swimming.
Anogenital warts belong to sexual health and are counselled separately.

quiz.q: How do you tell a plantar wart from a corn?
quiz.a: Wart: tender when squeezed from the sides, breaks the skin lines, black dots. Corn: tender on direct pressure, skin lines run through.

quiz.q: What are the black dots in a wart?

quiz.a: Salicylic acid daily after soaking and paring, for 8–12 weeks.

quiz.q: Who should not self-treat warts on the feet?
quiz.a: People with diabetes, peripheral neuropathy or vascular disease.

quiz.q: When is a ‘wart’ a red flag?
quiz.a: Rapid growth, bleeding, ulceration or atypical look, especially if immunosuppressed: consider SCC and refer.
